cosy-lesson.title: Dangerous Blindness: The Limit of Perspective

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Perspective – a particular attitude toward or way of regarding something.

p.em: Example: Traveling abroad gives you a completely new perspective on your own culture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Blindness – lack of perception, awareness, or judgment.

p.em: Example: Intellectual blindness prevents us from seeing alternative viewpoints.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bias – prejudice in favor of or against one thing, person, or group.

p.em: Example: Cognitive bias often distorts our logical decision-making.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reinforce – strengthen or support (an existing feeling, idea, or habit).

p.em: Example: Echo chambers on social media tend to reinforce our existing beliefs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Insular – ignorant of or uninterested in cultures, ideas, or peoples outside one's own.

p.em: Example: Living in an insular community can limit your intellectual growth.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fallacy – a mistaken belief, especially one based on unsound argument.

p.em: Example: His logical argument was actually built on a dangerous fallacy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Echo chamber – an environment where a person only encounters information that reflects their opinions.

p.em: Example: Social media algorithms construct an insular echo chamber.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intellect – the faculty of reasoning and understanding objectively.

p.em: Example: A sharp intellect requires the humility to admit mistakes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dogma – a principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.

p.em: Example: Healthy skepticism helps us question established religious or social dogma.

cosy-blockquote.p: Empathy – the ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

p.em: Example: Active listening is crucial for building deep empathy with opponents.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why is changing our perspective often the hardest intellectual task we face?
★ It is said that ideological blindness limits human perspective. How can we stay open?

Does intellectual blindness come from a lack of intelligence or a lack of humility?
★ Have you ever realized you were completely blind to a close friend's struggle?

How does cognitive bias protect us from uncomfortable truths about ourselves?
★ What is a personal bias you are actively trying to overcome?

Do search engine algorithms actively reinforce our existing beliefs?
★ Have you ever noticed your social feed showing only opinions you agree with?

Why do highly educated communities often develop an insular way of thinking?
★ Do you prefer stepping out of your social circle or staying in comfortable bubbles?

Can a highly logical argument still be built on a dangerous fallacy?
★ Tell us about a popular argument in the news that feels like a fallacy to you.

How does living in an online echo chamber affect our capacity for critical thinking?
★ What do you do to escape the echo chambers of the internet?

What is the difference between an intellectual debate and a noisy argument?
★ Do you enjoy engaging in intellectual debates with colleagues?

Why is a rigid dogma so attractive to people during times of global crisis?
★ Have you ever had to abandon a dogma you once believed in?

How can we practice active empathy toward someone we find politically extreme?
★ Is there someone in your life you struggle to show empathy to?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will enable us to view any situation from another person's perspective directly in virtual reality. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if you could instantly experience a stranger's thoughts?

As artificial intelligence advances, human intellectual blindness will be completely eliminated by objective machine analysis. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you trust an AI system to make your life decisions to avoid personal bias?

Future social platforms will warn users whenever their personal bias is influencing their comments. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use a browser extension that highlights your own cognitive biases?

Educational systems in 100 years will completely ban algorithms that reinforce individual opinions. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you send your children to a school that forces them to read opposing views daily?

Global digital networks will make insular communities impossible to maintain in tomorrow's world. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a community that is completely disconnected from the global web?

In the future, public debates will be moderated by AI systems designed to instantly flag any logical fallacy. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where machine logic controls all public discussions?

Escaping your digital echo chamber will become an expensive luxury rather than a simple choice. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you plan to protect your independent thinking in the next ten years?

Future societies will value an intellectual's capacity for admitting doubt far more than their academic credentials. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you nurture your own intellectual humility in a highly competitive world?

If future generations reject all forms of flexible thinking, they will experience a profound crisis of dogma. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What message about dogmatic thinking would you send to someone living 100 years from now?

A future world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the quiet mystery of emotional empathy. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of empathy, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: It is a blindness spot → Correct: It is a blind spot ((Idiomatic expression))
Incorrect: He is bias toward them → Correct: He is biased toward them ((Noun vs Adjective))
Incorrect: I am live in an echo chamber since years → Correct: I have lived in an echo chamber for years / I've been living in an echo chamber for years ((Present Perfect + Duration))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
